text:
Anna (CS): Heads-up team — I'm drafting a customer-facing note for Dedicated/Private customers in eu-west-1 where we've flagged intermittent ECC/XID and flaky GPU behavior on a small subset of cards. Need final wording and send plan by EOD. Draft below — please comment.

Anna (CS): ```Subject: Planned GPU maintenance & automatic failover for your Dedicated capacity

Hi <customer>,

We're contacting you because we've detected intermittent ECC/XID errors on a small number of GPU cards that back Dedicated and Private deployments in eu-west-1. To keep your applications reliable, our ops team will proactively drain the affected cards and replace them over the next 72 hours. During this process, traffic will be routed to healthy capacity automatically.

What to expect:
- Automatic failover to healthy GPUs when a card is drained (no model rollouts or config changes).
- Brief reconnects or transient latency increases for in-flight requests (expected single-digit to ~60s windows).
- No data migration is required and customer data will remain isolated.

What we're doing for you:
- Proactive drain of impacted GPUs and immediate routing to healthy capacity.
- Physical card replacement and post-replace validation.
- Continuous monitoring and a follow-up verification email once all replacements are complete.

Customer actions (recommended):
- No action needed for most setups.
- If you operate ultra low-latency real-time traffic, please reply to request a scheduled maintenance window so we can coordinate a quieter timeframe.

If you have any concerns or want a technical call to review failover behavior and runbooks, reply and we'll schedule one.

Regards,
Redwood Inference — Customer Success & Operations
```

Jon Infra: Couple of edits — please explicitly say "no model changes" (avoid "no model rollouts" confusion) and include the expected replacement window (we currently expect card swaps to happen between 02:00-06:00 UTC to minimize customer impact). Also add a short line about targeted customers who will get personalized email (we shouldn't broadcast to all Dedicated).

Mike Ops: Suggested subject alternatives and shortened blurb for high-sensitivity customers: 
- Subject short: "Planned GPU maintenance — automatic failover (eu-west-1)"
- Short blurb: "We're replacing a small number of faulty GPU cards; automatic failover will route traffic to healthy capacity. Expect brief reconnects; contact us to schedule a quieter window."

Priya (SRE): OpsBot created INC-2026-431 for the hardware replacement work. Runbook link: https://internal.redwood/infrarunbooks/gpu-hardware-drain (internal). Add the runbook link to the internal note and reference in the triage email.

Sara Eng: For Private installs, add this line: "If you run a Private deployment (customer-managed infra), your Redwood control plane will notify your on-prem agent to coordinate drain/replacement; we will not access customer data or infrastructure." Keeps expectations clear.

Jon Infra: Also call out SLAs — confirm no SLA credit impact for automatic routing events under our current Dedicated SLA wording. If there is a measurable impact we'll follow the standard incident/credit process and communicate separately.

Anna (CS): Updated draft below (short + long versions) and a per-audience send plan. Please review quickly.

Anna (CS): ```SHORT (for alerts channel / dashboard)
We're proactively replacing a small number of GPU cards in eu-west-1. Automatic failover will route traffic to healthy capacity; brief reconnects or transient latency increases may occur. Contact your CSM to schedule a maintenance window.

LONG (email to affected Dedicated/Private customers)
Subject: Planned GPU maintenance & automatic failover for your Dedicated capacity

Hi <customer>,

We wanted to let you know that we've detected intermittent hardware errors on a small subset of GPU cards in eu-west-1 that serve Dedicated and Private deployments. To keep your services reliable, our team will proactively drain the affected cards and replace them over the next 72 hours. Your traffic will be routed to healthy capacity automatically — there will be no changes to your deployed model versions or configuration.

What to expect:
- Automatic failover during drain.
- Brief reconnects or transient latency increases (most events < 60s).
- No customer data movement or exposure.

If you require a scheduled maintenance window or want a runbook walkthrough, reply to this email and we will set up a call.

We'll follow up after replacements and verification are complete.

Best regards,
Redwood Inference — Customer Success & Operations
```

Anna (CS): Send plan: 1) Personalized emails to 12 affected Dedicated tenants (CS to send after approval), 2) Short dashboard banner + in-product alert for any Private deployments in the region, 3) Post-incident follow-up email.

Mike Ops: Approved from ops side, please include the Ops on-call rotation and the INC-2026-431 reference in the internal send. Also prepare an ops slack bridge for any customers who request live coordination.

Priya (SRE): I'll schedule the swaps during 02:00-06:00 UTC windows and post a runbook step checklist in the incident. Observability will flag any unexpected error-rate delta > 5% as a priority.

OpsBot: Incident INC-2026-431 created and assigned to priya; priority P2; ETA for completion 72 hours.

Anna (CS): Thanks — with those approvals I'll finalize wording and send targeted emails in the next 90 minutes. If anyone sees a problem with the wording, flag now. :thumbsup:

Jon Infra: LGTM. Add a single sentence about reaching out to support@redwood.com for urgent issues.

Anna (CS): Added. Finalizing now and will post the short dashboard banner after emails go out.
